plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control: DE with n=3 power caveat
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 12000-gene x 6-sample raw Salmon gene-level count matrix from human liver, 3 drug-treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. The pipeline follows the grounded DESeq2 procedure: sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) to catch outliers/batch structure before any test; a minimal count pre-filter; the DESeq2 Wald test with the reference level explicitly set to 'control' and named contrast treated_vs_control; apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2 fold change; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2's independent filtering; and an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts/design as a second method, reporting the intersection of the two gene sets as the higher-confidence subset. Because the smallest group has only 3 replicates, both the model-design step and the DE step state the expected power limitation up front and the report restates it: at n=3/group, count-based DE tests recover only a minority of true positives, skewed toward large fold changes, and an absent gene is not evidence of no effect — the significance threshold is not loosened to compensate. Enrichment is done as GO (and Hallmark/Reactome) over-representation on the significant gene list (padj<0.05) with the tested genes as the explicit universe and up/down handled as stated lists, since the ORA rule set was selected by the knowledge service for a discrete-list enrichment question; if the significant list falls under ~50 genes (plausible at n=3/group) the enrichment step is instructed to fall back to fgsea preranked on the full ranked gene list (Wald statistic) instead, per the low-power flag. The count table lacks per-sample transcript-level Salmon quant files (already gene-summed), so the tximport length-offset step described by the knowledge service cannot be executed here; this is stated as a limitation rather than silently skipped, since the length-scaled offset mainly matters for isoform-usage confounds and DESeq2's median-of-ratios normalization on the gene counts remains valid without it. All steps ground on packages confirmed present in this sandbox (DESeq2 1.52.0, apeglm 1.34.0, edgeR 4.10.3, clusterProfiler 4.20.0, rrvgo 1.24.0, fgsea 1.38.0, org.Hs.eg.db 3.23.1) and reference gene sets confirmed present (MSigDB Hallmark human 2026.1, Reactome pathways current, MSigDB GO BP human 2026.1).

Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, alpha=0.05
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
DE report with power caveat at n=3/group, edgeR cross-check overlap, fit diagnostics, enrichment caveats
DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage
fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic with MSigDB Hallmark
